newsitem.title: USA: Former U.S. Senator Tsongas dead - CNN.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. Senator Tsongas dead - CNN.

text.p: Former U.S. senator and presidential candidate Paul Tsongas died on Saturday in a Massachusetts hospital, CNN reported.

Tsongas, a Democrat and former Massachusetts senator who ran for president in 1992, was 55. He died in Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, according to CNN. He had battled cancer for several years.
Tsongas, the son of a Greek immigrant father and an American-born mother who died when he was only seven years old, represented Massachusetts in the Senate from 1979 to 1985.
After retiring from the Senate to fight a deadly form of bone cancer, he fended off questions about his health by swimming competitively and entered a series of national meets.
Tsongas was admitted to the hospital Jan. 3 with liver and heart problems stemming from an an earlier bone marrow transplant, CNN said.
A graduate of Yale law school, Tsongas and his wife Niki have three daughters.
